standard.title: Plan and negotiate with others
standard.description: participate in activities that involve planning and negotiating with others, using modelled and idiomatic language, to agree, suggest and resolve
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and transact with others in familiar contexts using a range of phrases and modelled sentences (AC9LCH4C02). They can take on roles, give instructions, and participate in cultural presentations. They have not yet used idiomatic language in collaborative planning, negotiated competing preferences to reach resolution, or participated in community-facing collaborative projects.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in planning and negotiating activities using modelled and idiomatic language — making suggestions, resolving differences, reaching agreements — across collaborative tasks including community and school events.

nodes.label: Language for suggesting, agreeing and resolving
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the language of suggestion, agreement and resolution — including idiomatic expressions — to navigate collaborative decision-making.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least three language structures for suggesting, agreeing, or resolving in a collaborative planning task.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of planning and negotiation language — making suggestions, responding to suggestions, proposing alternatives, reaching agreement, resolving differences; include idiomatic expressions appropriate to the context; provide feedback on peers' contributions.
wider: Compare how suggestions and disagreements are managed in collaborative contexts in the target language community with Australian conventions — identify differences in directness, face-saving, and resolution strategies

Analyse the language of a target language negotiation or planning text — identify the structures used at each stage (proposal, response, counter-proposal, agreement) and discuss what makes them effective
nodes.hinge_reason: Language for suggestion, agreement and resolution is the functional prerequisite for all collaborative planning activity. Students who can only assert preferences without using negotiation language cannot participate meaningfully in the planning tasks this descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Negotiation language requires a bank of structures across different positions — suggesting, countering, conceding, agreeing. Repeated practice across varied collaborative contexts builds the flexible deployment needed for genuine negotiation.

success_criteria: Uses at least three structures for suggesting, agreeing, or resolving during a collaborative task
Reaches a negotiated outcome without abandoning the target language

nodes.label: Idiomatic language in collaborative contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use idiomatic expressions appropriate to collaborative and planning contexts, understanding that idiomatic meaning differs from literal meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two idiomatic expressions used in planning or collaborative contexts and use at least one correctly in context.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and use idiomatic expressions in collaborative planning contexts; understand that idiomatic meaning is not derived from literal word-for-word interpretation; discuss the social function of particular idioms in collaborative interaction.
wider: Research a set of idioms used in collaborative or persuasive contexts in the target language — explain their meaning, origin (where known), and compare with English equivalents or absence of equivalents
Compare how idioms are used differently in formal and informal collaborative contexts in the target language — identify when idiomatic language is appropriate and when it would be inappropriate

response_modes.reason: Idiomatic language is understood and deployed through varied contextual encounters — the same idiom used in different registers, situations and with different speakers. Varied exposure across collaborative contexts builds genuine understanding beyond memorised definitions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners often know idioms from home without being able to explain or examine them. Width investment here allows students to make explicit the idiomatic knowledge they bring — building metalinguistic awareness of a dimension of the target language that is often invisible to more formal learners.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two idiomatic expressions used in collaborative contexts
Uses at least one idiom correctly in a collaborative or planning exchange

nodes.label: Collaborative planning for real outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collaborate to plan and execute a shared project or event — making decisions, dividing tasks, and resolving differences — using target language throughout the planning process.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in planning a shared project or event, contributing at least three target language turns to the planning discussion, including at least one suggestion and one response to a peer's idea.
nodes.typical_width: Collaborate to plan school events, community presentations, campaigns or projects — making decisions, assigning roles, negotiating content, resolving disagreements; use target language throughout; contribute to real or simulated community-facing outcomes.
wider: Lead the planning process for a collaborative project — facilitating discussion, managing disagreement, and bringing the group to a shared outcome using target language
Evaluate the planning process after completion — identify what language moves were most effective in reaching resolution and what would be improved in a future collaborative task

response_modes.reason: Collaborative planning for real outcomes integrates negotiation language (node 1) and idiomatic expression (node 2) into a sustained, purposeful activity. The teaching investment is in creating genuine stakes — real projects, real decisions — that require authentic negotiation rather than simulated practice.

success_criteria: Contributes at least three target language turns to a planning discussion including at least one suggestion
Helps reach a shared decision through target language interaction without abandoning the language
